summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy and PEG dependence, and a history of osteonecrosis was readmitted for tachypnea and coffee-ground emesis. He had recently been discharged after treatment for pseudomonal UTI. Evaluation revealed leukocytosis and elevated lactate, with concern for aspiration pneumonitis due to inappropriate oral intake at rehab. Chest imaging showed chronic interstitial lung disease without new consolidation. He improved with supportive care, including suctioning and nebulizers, and did not require antibiotic escalation despite Pseudomonas growth in sputum. A brief SVT episode resolved with vagal maneuvers. Trazodone was discontinued after contributing to altered mental status. Pain from chronic osteonecrosis was managed with acetaminophen. He stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged back to rehabilitation with updated orders for NPO status and medication adjustments.
